name: Hmong Don
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. Open access, ANU Open Research hdl 1885/146760
sources.note: Comparative, family-level only; does not mention Hmong Don. p. 11: 'All Hmong-Mien languages are tonal, and the primary function of tone is lexical discrimination.' The only stress remark (p. 28) concerns Mienic: quoting Downer 1961:539 on Mien reduced syllables having 'weaker stress and shorter duration than the following full syllables so that a strong iambic rhythm is imparted to disyllabic words'. Nothing on word stress in Hmongic.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Dallas: SIL. Entry 'Hmong Don' (hmf), web version archived 2010
sources.note: 'Comments: Tonal, 7 tones.' Region 'Ha Giang Province, Hua Binh, YenBai, Nghia Lo'; classification Hmong-Mien, Hmongic, Chuanqiandian; no population estimate. No stress statement. (Current ethnologue.com entry could not be reached by automated download.)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page hmon1263 'Hmong Don' (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank)
sources.note: Database page only. References: Nguyễn Văn Lợi 1972 (overview; minimal), Niederer 1998:310-311 (subclassification comment), Eberhard et al. 2025 (AES status 6a*). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Hmong language' and Wikipedia (vi) 'Tiếng H'Mông', 'Người H'Mông'
sources.note: Tertiary. en: Hmong Don (hmf) and Hmong Dô (hmv) are Vietnamese varieties 'not very well classified', 'very poorly known', no population estimates; no stress discussion. vi 'Người H'Mông': Vietnamese subgroups Hmông Trắng (Hmoob Dawb/Đơưz), Hmông Hoa, Hmông Đỏ (Hmoob Lees), Hmông Đen (Hmoob Dub/Đuz), Hmông Xanh, Na Miểu; Yên Bái mainly Hmông Hoa and Hmông Đỏ; no references given for the classification.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed. Entry 'Hmong Don' (hmf). Dallas: SIL International.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: needed for identity, not expected to state stress.

sources.citation: Phùng Thị Thanh. 2007. Phân tích đối chiếu hệ thống ngữ âm - âm vị học tiếng Việt với tiếng Hmông và các lỗi phát âm tiếng Việt của học sinh Hmông. PhD dissertation (LATS Ngữ văn 62.22.01.01), Viện Ngôn ngữ học, Hà Nội.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: A full contrastive phonology of Vietnamese and Hmong (tones, initials, rimes); the most complete modern phonology of Hmong in Vietnam found. Whether it treats the Hmong Đen/Đu variety (hmf) or Hmong Lềnh/Trắng must be checked; likely to state whether Hmong has word stress. Full text held in the National Library of Vietnam thesis database (login required).

sources.citation: Nguyễn Văn Hiệu. 2004. Ngữ vị từ trong tiếng Mông (Có vị từ hành động và vị từ trạng thái làm trung tâm). PhD dissertation, ĐH Khoa học Xã hội và Nhân văn, Hà Nội, 207 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Grammar of Hmong (Vietnam) verb phrases; introductory chapter may summarize the phonology (syllable, tone, stress) of the variety described. Full text login-only at the National Library of Vietnam.

sources.citation: Niederer, Barbara. 1998. Les langues Hmong-Mjen (Miáo-Yáo): phonologie historique. Munich: Lincom Europa. (pp. 310-311 cited by Glottolog for hmf subclassification)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Glottolog's only other reference for hmf; comparative-historical phonology whose pp. 310-311 comment on the placement of the Vietnamese Hmong varieties. Useful for identity; unlikely to state word stress.

sources.citation: Enwall, Joakim. 1995. Hmong Writing Systems in Vietnam: A Case Study of Vietnam's Minority Language Policy. Stockholm: Center for Pacific Asia Studies, Stockholm University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Reviews the Vietnamese classification of Hmong dialects (Nguyễn Văn Lợi's Hmong Đơ/Đu/Lềnh/Sí/Sua) underlying the hmf/hmv codes; needed to pin the identity of 'Hmong Don' = Hmông Đen (Hmoob Dub); not a phonology.

sources.citation: Nguyễn Văn Lợi. 1972. 'Một số nét về tiếng Mèo ở Việt Nam'. In Tìm hiểu ngôn ngữ các dân tộc thiểu số ở Việt Nam, vol. 1, 139-171. Hà Nội: Viện Ngôn ngữ học.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only Glottolog-linked description for hmf (and hmv); a 33-page Vietnamese overview of the Hmong dialects of Vietnam ('Hmong Du' = Hmong Don). Vietnamese-tradition phonetic overviews routinely comment on trọng âm; this is the primary candidate for a first-hand statement.
